newsitem.title: UK: Bridport sees acquisitions boosting EPS.
newsitem.headline: Bridport sees acquisitions boosting EPS.

text.p: Bridport-Gundry Plc said on Wednesday it expected its three most recent acquisitions to add about 10 to 20 percent to its annualised earnings per share in the first 12 months after their completion.
"They're clearly earnings enhancing," chief executive Geoffrey Woods told journalists at a lunch.

Earlier, the maker of aviation and defence products said it conditionally agreed to buy Militair Aviation Ltd, Avery Flight International Ltd, and Safetywear Ltd for a total of about 11.95 million stg.
The company also said it plans a three-for-four rights issue to raise 9.1 million stg.
Company executives said the three acquisitions were expected to be completed in December.

The company projected that Militair, a supplier of military aircraft parts, would have an earnings potential of 850,000 to 1.25 million stg of annualised pretax profits in the 12-month period after the deal's completion.
Avery, a maker of airline cabin textile products, was expected to add 600,000 to 800,000 stg to annualised pretax profits, while the target for Safetywear was roughly 130,000.

Bridport-Gundry reported pretax profits of 1.45 million stg on turnover of 30.3 million stg for the year ended July 31, compared to 1.34 million stg and 28.4 million stg, respectively, for the prior year.
The company said it did not expect to take any exceptional charges for the acquisitions outside of normal trading expenses.
After the acquisitions, the company said its aviation and defence businesses would make up over 75 percent of its pretax profits compared to the current level of more than 50 percent.
Woods said the company expected to dispose of its sports and leisure division, as well as certain industrial product businesses, over the next year or two.

"We'll now look to find ways in which we can move them on," he said, adding the divisions to be disposed of accounted for some 50 percent of the company's turnover but only about 20 percent of its pretax profits.
The company also planned to retain its medical division, which made up some 30 percent of its pretax profits, and increase its focus on its aviation and defence businesses.
"We are focusing on aviation because it is a growth area," chairman David Sebire said.
Bridport-Gundry's shares jumped 7p to 149-1/2p in afternoon trade.
